case_outputs.problem_frame: Diagnose why a historically stable three-stage sales process is now expected to shift from growth to decline, separating volume, conversion, productivity, and external demand effects across prospect list, sales script, and pitch delivery.
candidate_axes: Sales funnel stage: prospect list, sales script, pitch delivery
Performance metric: lead volume, lead quality, conversion rate, deal size, sales cycle, rep productivity
Cause type: internal execution, market/customer change, competitive pressure, forecast/model artifact
case_outputs.selected_axis_rationale: The funnel-stage axis maps directly to the operating process the company understands, keeps the tree mutually exclusive at the first level, and makes the first research pass easy to assign to available data owners.
full_tree: Sales decline expectation is real or a forecasting artifact
Prospect list coverage no longer matches addressable market
Prospect list refresh rate is too slow
Prospect source mix has shifted toward lower-intent leads
Script message no longer fits current customer needs
Script fails to differentiate against competitors
Script is too complex or creates objections
Script compliance has changed across reps
Script testing and iteration cadence is inadequate
Rep skill or tenure mix has worsened
Pricing or offer economics have worsened
Customer budget cycles or purchasing criteria changed
pruned_tree: Sales decline expectation is real or a forecasting artifact
Prospect list deterioration
Prospect list volume or quality has fallen
Prospect source mix has shifted toward lower-intent leads
Sales script deterioration
Script message no longer fits customer needs or competition
Script compliance varies across reps
Pitch delivery deterioration
Rep activity volume, consistency, or follow-up discipline has fallen
Rep skill or tenure mix has worsened
External or structural headwinds
Demand, competition, pricing, or buying criteria changed
sibling_logic: First-level branches separate the three controlled sales-process stages from external/forecast factors.
Within each stage, branches separate input quantity, input quality, execution quality, and fit-to-market causes.
The pruned tree keeps hypotheses that can explain a forward-looking decline despite long historical stability and that are measurable in a first pass.

leaf_tasks.research_question: Is the expected decline visible in actual leading indicators, or is it driven by a change in forecast assumptions?
evidence_requirements: Historical monthly sales, pipeline, conversion, and forecast data
Forecast model version history and assumption changes
Comparison of forecast decline timing to observed leading-indicator changes
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: One-page bridge from historical growth to expected decline, split into actual trend vs model-assumption effect.
disconfirming_evidence: Observed lead, conversion, and close-rate trends remain stable while only forecast assumptions changed
Forecast model changes fully explain the decline without operational deterioration

leaf_tasks.research_question: Has prospect list volume, quality, or source mix deteriorated enough to explain the sales gap?
evidence_requirements: Lead counts by month and source
Lead-to-opportunity and opportunity-to-close rates by source
ICP fit, firmographic, or intent-score trends
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Prospect-list diagnostic table quantifying volume, quality, and source-mix contribution to expected sales decline.
disconfirming_evidence: Lead volume and quality are stable or improving
Source mix changes have no material conversion or deal-size effect

leaf_tasks.research_question: Has the sales script lost message-market fit or competitive differentiation?
evidence_requirements: Current and prior script versions
Win/loss notes, objection logs, call transcripts, customer feedback
Competitive messaging and offer comparison
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Script-fit assessment showing top objections, message gaps, and estimated conversion impact.
disconfirming_evidence: Objection patterns and script adherence are unchanged
Conversion decline occurs equally where script is not used or across all script variants

leaf_tasks.research_question: Has pitch delivery degraded through lower activity, weaker rep mix, inconsistent execution, or follow-up gaps?
evidence_requirements: Rep-level activity, connect, demo, proposal, and follow-up metrics
Rep tenure, training, territory, and quota assignment data
Call scoring or manager QA results
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Rep execution variance analysis identifying whether decline is broad-based or concentrated in specific teams, cohorts, or behaviors.
disconfirming_evidence: Activity and QA metrics are stable by rep cohort
Decline is uniform across reps despite stable execution metrics

leaf_tasks.research_question: Are external demand, competitive, pricing, or purchasing changes causing the expected decline?
evidence_requirements: Market demand indicators and customer budget data
Competitor win-rate trends and pricing changes
Deal loss reasons and buyer decision criteria over time
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: External-headwind memo ranking market, competition, pricing, and buyer-change hypotheses by explanatory power.
disconfirming_evidence: Loss reasons and market demand indicators are stable
Decline appears only in internally controlled stages while comparable market benchmarks remain healthy

pruning_decisions: Deferred deep territory-design analysis until first-pass data shows prospect coverage or rep assignment problems.
Deferred detailed compensation analysis because the prompt centers on a simple stable process and first-pass funnel diagnostics are higher-yield.
Deferred CRM tooling analysis unless activity, follow-up, or data-integrity evidence points to operational system failure.
quality_gate_results: MECE check: first-level branches cover process stages plus external/model factors with limited overlap.
Diagnostic usefulness check: every retained leaf can be tested with sales funnel, CRM, call, or market evidence.
Pruning check: retained plan prioritizes hypotheses most likely to explain a growth-to-decline inflection in a stable process.

case_outputs.problem_frame: Develop an energy-cost reduction strategy for a factory by separating cost drivers into demand reduction, unit-cost reduction, structural production choices, incentives, and organizational enablers.
candidate_axes: Cost equation: energy consumption volume, unit price, incentives/rebates, allocation of production load
Intervention type: operating practices, low-capital engineering, major capital, sourcing/fuel mix, organization
Time horizon and capital intensity: immediate no/low capex, medium-term engineering, long-term strategic capital
case_outputs.selected_axis_rationale: The cost-equation axis is the cleanest top-down tree because it starts from energy cost mechanics, then nests the candidate topics under the lever they affect. It avoids mixing initiatives, enablers, and outcomes at the same level.
full_tree: Shutdown, startup, idle, and standby discipline
Setpoint, temperature, pressure, and speed optimization
Preventive maintenance and leak loss control
Insulation, steam traps, compressed-air leaks, and heat recovery fixes
Motor, drive, pump, and fan optimization
Controls tuning, sensors, metering, and automation upgrades
High-efficiency boilers, furnaces, chillers, compressors, or ovens
Building or line retrofit requiring shutdown planning
Switch between electricity, gas, steam, biomass, waste heat, or alternative fuels
Supplier, tariff, hedging, and demand-charge optimization
Power purchase agreements or renewable procurement
Tax credits, rebates, grants, carbon credits, and demand-response payments
Compliance with eligibility, measurement, and reporting requirements
Move products to lower-energy-cost mills or lines
Balance freight, labor, yield, quality, capacity, and customer service tradeoffs
Energy governance, owner accountability, and KPI cadence
Capital approval process and project pipeline management
Energy management system, metering, analytics, and audit routines
Training, incentives, and cross-functional operating model
pruned_tree: Reduce total factory energy cost
Reduce energy consumption volume
Operating practices with immediate savings potential
Shutdown, idle, scheduling, setpoint, and maintenance discipline
Low-capital engineering with fast payback
Leaks, insulation, heat recovery, motor/drive, controls, and auxiliary-load fixes
Reduce unit energy price
Fuel mix and tariff/load-shifting opportunities
Sourcing, contract, demand-charge, and hedging optimization
Capture government incentives tied to eligible projects
Change product-to-mill assignments where energy-cost differences are material
Build organizational capability needed to sustain and scale savings
sibling_logic: First-level branches map to the energy-cost equation: consumed volume, unit price, incentives, production allocation, and execution capability.
Operating practices, low-capital engineering, and major capital are nested under consumption reduction because they primarily reduce energy intensity or waste.
Organization is treated as an enabler, retained in the pruned tree only where it affects sustainment, measurement, and project throughput.

leaf_tasks.research_question: Where is the current energy-cost baseline concentrated by utility, process, line, product, time period, and mill?
evidence_requirements: Utility bills, interval meter data, and tariffs for at least 12 to 24 months
Production volumes, product mix, line schedules, and operating hours
Submetering or engineering estimates by process where direct metering is absent
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Energy cost baseline and Pareto showing cost by source, process, product, and time with normalized energy intensity.
disconfirming_evidence: Energy costs are too evenly distributed for focused intervention
Metering gaps prevent attribution and require a measurement plan before initiative ranking

leaf_tasks.research_question: Which operating-practice changes can reduce energy use immediately without material capital or quality risk?
evidence_requirements: Shutdown/startup logs, equipment idle time, schedules, setpoints, maintenance records
Operator procedures and adherence audits
Energy consumption during production vs non-production periods
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: No/low-capex operating savings list with savings estimate, implementation owner, risk, and required behavior change.
disconfirming_evidence: Most consumption is process-theoretical minimum or production-linked with little idle waste
Operational changes create unacceptable throughput, quality, or safety risk

leaf_tasks.research_question: Which low-capital engineering projects have the fastest payback and lowest execution risk?
evidence_requirements: Engineering audit of steam, compressed air, motors, pumps, fans, heat recovery, controls, HVAC, and lighting
Capex and implementation timing estimates
Measured or benchmarked savings factors and maintenance constraints
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Ranked low-capex project pipeline with cost, savings, payback, downtime need, and confidence level.
disconfirming_evidence: Savings are small relative to capital and downtime
Root causes require major capital rather than low-capital fixes

leaf_tasks.research_question: Are unit-price levers large enough to prioritize sourcing, fuel mix, tariff, load-shifting, or hedging actions?
evidence_requirements: Tariff structures, contract terms, demand charges, hourly prices, fuel prices, and supplier options
Load profiles and operational flexibility by process
Constraints from equipment, emissions permits, reliability, and product quality
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Unit-price opportunity assessment separating contract savings, demand-charge savings, fuel-switching economics, and load-shift feasibility.
disconfirming_evidence: Existing contracts and tariffs are already optimized
Load is inflexible and fuel switching is uneconomic or operationally constrained

leaf_tasks.research_question: Do government incentives materially change the economics or sequencing of energy projects?
evidence_requirements: Applicable federal, state, utility, and local incentive programs
Eligibility rules, deadlines, measurement requirements, and application burden
Project list mapped to qualifying technologies and baseline requirements
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Incentive map and project-adjusted payback analysis.
disconfirming_evidence: Incentives are unavailable, too small, expired, or incompatible with likely projects
Compliance cost exceeds expected benefit

leaf_tasks.research_question: Would product-to-mill or product-to-line reassignment lower system cost after energy, freight, labor, yield, capacity, and service tradeoffs?
evidence_requirements: Energy intensity and tariff differences by mill or line
Product routing, capacity, changeover, labor, yield, quality, freight, and customer-service data
Network constraints and production planning rules
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Product assignment model showing net margin impact by reassignment scenario.
disconfirming_evidence: Energy savings are offset by freight, yield, labor, capacity, or service penalties
Constraints prevent meaningful reassignment

leaf_tasks.research_question: What organization and governance changes are required to sustain savings and execute the project pipeline?
evidence_requirements: Current energy ownership, KPI cadence, capital approval workflow, and maintenance accountability
Metering, analytics, and reporting capabilities
Prior energy project execution history and sustainment results
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Energy management operating model with owners, KPIs, review cadence, and project governance.
disconfirming_evidence: Existing governance already sustains verified savings
Savings are mainly one-time commercial renegotiations requiring little operating-model change

pruning_decisions: Major capital projects are included in the full tree but excluded from first-pass pruned research unless baseline and low-capex work show a large residual gap, because they require more engineering detail and longer payback validation.
Organization is pruned to sustainment and execution capability, not treated as a standalone savings bucket.
Government incentives are retained only as an economics modifier for eligible projects, avoiding a disconnected incentives workstream.
quality_gate_results: MECE check: consumption, price, incentives, product allocation, and organizational sustainment are separated by how they affect total cost.
Candidate coverage check: all user-provided topics appear in the full tree and the pruned tree retains first-pass high-yield topics.
Research-plan check: leaf tasks produce decision artifacts needed to rank initiatives by savings, cost, risk, and timing.

case_outputs.problem_frame: Evaluate whether a new shorter curing process can lower marginal cost for a manufactured product by separating direct variable-cost changes, throughput and utilization effects, quality/yield effects, and implementation constraints.
candidate_axes: Cost equation: material, labor, energy, scrap/rework, overhead absorption, capacity opportunity cost
Process step: pre-cure preparation, curing, post-cure handling, inspection/rework
Decision lens: technical feasibility, economic impact, operational risk, customer/regulatory acceptance
case_outputs.selected_axis_rationale: The cost-equation axis best fits a marginal-cost question. A shorter curing process matters economically only through variable inputs, cycle time, yield, quality, and capacity effects, so the tree should quantify those pathways directly.
full_tree: Shorter curing process lowers marginal cost
Material consumption per good unit changes
Catalyst, additive, coating, or consumable use changes
Energy consumption per batch or unit changes
Packaging, handling, or WIP carrying cost changes
Batch size or scheduling flexibility improves
WIP inventory and queue time decrease
Overtime, expediting, or outsourced production decreases
Fixed overhead absorption per unit improves where capacity constrained
Quality and yield economics improve or deteriorate
Customer returns, warranty, or field failures change
Implementation cost and operating constraints affect net savings
Scale-up feasibility from pilot to production
Ability to meet demand or reduce lead time
Risk of cannibalizing premium quality positioning
pruned_tree: Shorter curing process lowers marginal cost
Direct variable input cost changes
Material, consumable, labor, and energy cost per good unit
Throughput and utilization economics improve
Cycle time, bottleneck capacity, WIP, overtime, and outsourcing impact
Quality and yield economics improve or deteriorate
First-pass yield, scrap, rework, inspection, and product-performance impact
Implementation and qualification costs affect net savings
Equipment, downtime, validation, safety, regulatory, and customer approval costs
Scale-up feasibility determines whether pilot economics hold in production
sibling_logic: First-level branches distinguish economic benefit mechanisms from offsetting risk and implementation costs.
Direct inputs capture marginal cost per attempted unit, while quality/yield converts attempted-unit cost into cost per good unit.
Throughput is retained because shorter cure time may reduce marginal cost indirectly when curing is the bottleneck or avoids premium capacity costs.

leaf_tasks.research_question: What is the current marginal cost baseline per good unit for the existing curing process?
evidence_requirements: Bill of materials, consumables, labor routing, energy usage, scrap/rework, and inspection cost
Cycle time, batch size, utilization, and bottleneck data
Current yield and cost accounting rules
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Current-state marginal cost model per good unit with sensitivity to yield, cycle time, energy, and labor.
disconfirming_evidence: Curing contributes immaterial cost or bottleneck effect
Cost accounting cannot separate marginal cost from allocated fixed overhead without additional data

leaf_tasks.research_question: How does the shorter curing process change direct material, consumable, labor, and energy use per good unit?
evidence_requirements: Pilot or engineering trial input usage by batch
Energy meter or equipment power data under old and new process
Labor observation or routing estimates for changed handling steps
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Side-by-side variable-input cost comparison for old vs new curing process.
disconfirming_evidence: Shorter cure requires expensive additives or consumables that offset energy/labor savings
Observed input usage variance is larger than estimated savings

leaf_tasks.research_question: Does shorter curing increase effective capacity or reduce premium operating costs?
evidence_requirements: Process flow map and bottleneck analysis
Demand, utilization, overtime, expediting, and outsourcing history
Cycle-time and queue-time measurements from trials
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Capacity value model showing marginal-cost impact under unconstrained, constrained, and growth-demand scenarios.
disconfirming_evidence: Curing is not the bottleneck and capacity has slack
Reduced cure time does not change staffing, overtime, outsourcing, or production schedule

leaf_tasks.research_question: Does the shorter curing process preserve or improve first-pass yield, scrap, rework, and product performance?
evidence_requirements: Trial yield, defect, scrap, and rework data
Lab tests for strength, durability, dimensional stability, finish, and other critical-to-quality attributes
Accelerated aging or stress-test results where relevant
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Quality economics report translating yield and performance changes into cost per good unit and risk-adjusted savings.
disconfirming_evidence: Yield declines enough to offset cycle-time or input savings
Performance failures appear in accelerated tests or customer-critical specifications

leaf_tasks.research_question: What one-time and recurring implementation costs are required to run the shorter process reliably?
evidence_requirements: Equipment modification estimates, downtime plan, validation requirements, SOP updates, training, maintenance impacts
Safety, environmental, and regulatory review
Customer qualification or specification-change requirements
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Implementation economics and payback schedule distinguishing one-time conversion cost from recurring marginal-cost changes.
disconfirming_evidence: Validation or qualification cost overwhelms savings over the product life
Safety, regulatory, or customer requirements block adoption

leaf_tasks.research_question: Do pilot results scale to normal production conditions across products, lines, operators, and seasons?
evidence_requirements: Pilot design, sample size, run conditions, operator mix, equipment settings, and production-scale trial data
Variance analysis across batches, shifts, raw-material lots, and ambient conditions
Control limits and process capability metrics
leaf_tasks.expected_artifact: Scale-up risk assessment with required production trial design and decision thresholds.
disconfirming_evidence: Pilot was run under non-representative conditions
Process variance increases materially at production scale

pruning_decisions: Deferred broader commercial pricing analysis because the stated objective is marginal cost, with commercial effects relevant only after technical and cost feasibility are established.
Deferred full network optimization unless capacity value proves material beyond the single product/process scope.
Deferred deep supplier renegotiation work unless the shorter process depends on new materials or formulation changes.
quality_gate_results: MECE check: branches separate direct cost, throughput value, quality/yield, implementation cost, and scale-up risk.
Decision usefulness check: each task feeds a go/no-go economics model for the shorter curing process.

Pruning check: first-pass plan focuses on hypotheses that can overturn the cost-saving claim quickly: immaterial baseline, offsetting input costs, no bottleneck value, yield loss, qualification cost, or failed scale-up.
